clue.text: Furious protest before the French murderer returns

indicators.note: the protest word comes first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: returns tells us the French article and the murderer are read backwards

parts.note: la is the French feminine 'the'
Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A furious protest is staged before a French murderer is sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses LACAIN to give NIACAL after DEMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoniacal behaviour is frenzied and possessed, a close synonym of raging or furious.

clue.text: Paint a hunk of a nudist emperor

indicators.note: a hunk is a chunk cut out, so the letters come from inside the words nudist emperor

explanation.surface: A painting of part of a naked emperor, a nod to the Emperor's New Clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a kind of water-based paint used on walls and for scenery.

clue.text: Weary spymaster returns with warrant

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

indicators.note: returns says the word for weary is read backwards

parts.note: to weary is to tire

explanation.surface: A tired spy chief comes home bearing a warrant.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve or justify it, as to warrant does.

clue.text: I disagree with Blair over ballot box — yell harshly? Never!

parts.note: no is what you say when you disagree
Tony Blair, former UK prime minister
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
an urn is a vessel into which votes are cast

indicators.note: harshly suggests the word yell is treated roughly and reshaped

explanation.surface: A voter rejects Blair and, at the ballot box, refuses to shout harshly about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harshly' rearranges YELL into ELLY. 'Not on your nelly' is British slang for an emphatic 'certainly not'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular British refusal meaning absolutely not, an exclamation like the clue's.

clue.text: One flies along a road over hill

indicators.note: in a down entry, the road part sits over, above, the hill

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in the Appian Way
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone flies along a road above a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot of an aircraft is one who flies, so this is a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Badly garble a calculation with symbols

indicators.note: badly says the letters of garble and a are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: Someone has messed up a sum involving symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is the branch of mathematics in which letters and symbols stand for numbers.

clue.text: It might be used for dressing tots when bawling

definitions.text: It might be used for dressing

indicators.note: bawling is crying out, so the word is spoken out and we enter a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to tot up is to add, so tots means adds

explanation.surface: Something might be used to dress small children who are howling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tots' is a verb (totting up figures), not small children; 'dressing' is shaping timber.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a carpenter's tool used for dressing, or rough-shaping, wood.

clue.text: Do this and you might see how I go back in time

parts.words: Do this and you might see how
parts.note: doctor means rearrange, so doctoring the word who produces the word how seen in the clue

explanation.surface: Someone explains how to travel back in time.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: doctor (alter) WHO and you get HOW. The definition is the time-travelling television Doctor speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC television hero travels through history in the TARDIS, so the time traveller speaks of himself.

clue.text: Did BS characters' followers get cast out?

wordplay.reading: D I D B S each moved one letter on

parts.note: the letters that follow D, I, D, B and S in the alphabet are E, J, E, C and T

explanation.surface: A question about whether the disciples of some dodgy characters were thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take each letter of DIDBS and replace it with the next letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject someone is to throw or expel them out, the same as casting them out.

clue.text: Clumsy pub landlord's partner Seth dancing jig

parts.note: Al Murray is the British comedian known as The Pub Landlord
a lover is a partner

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters of Seth jumping about

parts.note: to jig is to hop about

explanation.surface: The landlord's clumsy partner Seth dances a jig in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges SETH to THES. 'All over the shop' is British slang for in a mess, disorganised.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all over the shop is haphazard and uncoordinated, which is close to clumsy.

clue.text: Remove their guns, OK?

indicators.note: read as re-move, moving the letters of their guns around again

explanation.surface: A demand that someone be disarmed, checking it is agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure thing is an informal American way of saying yes, certainly, all right.

clue.text: Entice Conservative inside with sordid cash

indicators.note: inside places the Conservative letter within the word for entice

parts.note: to entice is to lure

explanation.surface: A Tory is enticed with dirty money.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Filthy lucre' is money regarded as tainted, so the word means sordid gain.

clue.text: Can court after former partner's gone

indicators.note: can and court come after the former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A legal fight goes to court once an ex-partner has left.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct species has died out completely, so it is gone for good.

clue.text: Attack includes small explosion

indicators.note: includes says the attack word holds the small word inside it

parts.note: a bout is an attack, as of illness
low means small, as in a low number

explanation.surface: An assault involves a minor explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowout is a sudden burst, as of a tyre or an oil well, an explosion.

clue.text: A moral purge scuppered indoor entertainment

indicators.note: a scuppered plan is wrecked, so the letters of a moral purge are broken up

explanation.surface: A campaign of moral cleansing ruined some indoor fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades and similar games played in a sitting room are entertainment indoors.

clue.text: Get back using transport around City area

indicators.note: around says the transport word goes round the City letters

parts.note: transport in the sense of ecstasy, rapture
EC is the postcode area for the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone regains something by taking transport through the City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' is ecstasy here, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapture is to take back or regain, so it means to get back.

clue.text: You and I would take the plunge

definitions.meaning: contracted, you and I would is ..., the same letters without the apostrophe
an idiom for committing oneself, especially to marriage

explanation.surface: We would both take the risk together.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the plunge is a stock idiom for getting married, and to marry is the verb wanted.

clue.text: Stain round object coloured it

parts.note: a disc is a flat round object
red, as in having coloured or blushed

explanation.surface: A round thing gets stained when someone colours it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain on someone's reputation is a discredit to them.

clue.text: Crash heard in miniature car park

indicators.note: in miniature means made smaller, so the spoken word is cut short by a letter; the answer also sits hidden in 'miniature car', a deliberate extra route and not a coincidence
heard means the word for crash is spoken, and we write a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a wreck is a crash; the answer also sits hidden in 'miniature car', a deliberate second route and not a coincidence

explanation.surface: A collision happens in a tiny car park.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple clue: 'Crash heard' sounds the answer, it is hidden in 'miniature car', and 'park' defines it. A rec is a British recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for recreation ground, the local public park or playing field in Britain.

clue.text: It's in Europe and it's horribly dull

indicators.note: horribly says the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: it's is read as it, with 's (is) in a linking role

explanation.surface: Someone complains that Europe is dreadfully boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges IT, EUROPE and ITS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repetitious keeps going over the same ground and so is tedious and dull.

clue.text: Present lecturer's iron rule

parts.note: prof, short for professor, a university lecturer
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
R is an abbreviation for rule, from rex/regina

explanation.surface: A professor offers his iron rule as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To proffer is to hold out or offer, which is to present something.

clue.text: Willing to examine mischievous goddess

parts.note: to examine is to test
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to question a troublesome goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' means having made a will, not eager.
explanation.definitionFit: A testate person has left a valid will, so is willing in the legal sense.

clue.text: What's happening about Farah's boss?

parts.note: 'sup is slang for what's up, what's happening
re means about, concerning
Mo Farah, British Olympic distance runner

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is going on with Mo Farah's boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge, the head or chief.

clue.text: Occupy building as seen in street

indicators.note: seen in places the word for as within the street abbreviation

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of

explanation.surface: Taking over a building as it appears on a street.
explanation.definitionFit: To squat is to occupy an empty property without permission.

clue.text: Poet and writers in series

indicators.note: in puts the writers inside the series abbreviation

parts.note: pens are things that write

explanation.surface: A poet and some authors appear in a book series.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Part of flight from a prison's over

indicators.note: over says the article shifts across, moving to a new place in the prison word

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Someone's time in jail is over, a flight from prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' moves A from the front of ASTIR to give STAIR; 'flight' is a flight of stairs, not an escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made up of individual steps, each one a stair.

clue.text: In America, rural Republicans aren't seen as common

parts.note: US is the United States, America

indicators.note: aren't seen tells us letters disappear from the word rural

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican, here two of them

explanation.surface: Rural Republicans in the US are not regarded as vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing both Rs from RURAL leaves UAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual means ordinary or customary, as common does.

clue.text: Rolls possibly Dutch learning aid

parts.note: a Rolls-Royce is an example of a flash car

explanation.surface: Perhaps Dutch bread rolls help someone learn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' is the Rolls-Royce car, not bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A card shown briefly to drill vocabulary or facts is a classroom learning aid.

clue.text: Hiker turning back makes it appear it's a long hike

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the two words make the letters appear, showing them inside

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A walker who turns round makes the journey look longer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took all of 'makes it appear it's a long hike' as the definition; 'makes it appear' is the hidden-word signal, so the definition is just 'long hike'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is an arduous journey on foot, a long hike.

clue.text: Bohemian going begging with whisky, perhaps

parts.note: something going begging is available for nothing, free
whisky is an example of a spirit

explanation.surface: A Bohemian gets whisky that nobody wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A free spirit lives unconventionally, like a Bohemian artist.
